name: sha256
algorithm: SHA-256 hashing over a generated multi-MiB SplitMix64 buffer: bulk_reps full-buffer passes plus short_reps passes over 64-byte slices, XOR-folding the first 8 little-endian bytes of every digest into a u64 checksum (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses bitwise XOR and wrapping SplitMix64; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares standard library SHA-256 implementations (including hardware SHA-NI dispatch where the std provides it); XOR-folding every digest checks that every implementation produced identical SHA-256 outputs
notes: Combines both bulk throughput (bulk_reps full-buffer passes over mib MiB) and short-message overhead (short_reps passes hashing every 64-byte slice), mutating one buffer byte after each pass so no hash can be hoisted.

Mk's std.hash.Sha256, Go's crypto/sha256, and .NET's System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256 (Windows CNG) may use CPU SHA extensions at run time; Zig's std.crypto.hash.sha2.Sha256 compiles for the row's x86-64-v2 target.
